Dear All,

This is a bit embarrassing because I presume that there is a very easy solution but I can't come up with it.
I have count data on waterbirds and some environmental covariates and also some other covariates regarding the "sampling effort". And I want to ran

pcountOpen(~1, ~1, ~1, ~1, um.dat.covs, mixture="NB",dynamics="trend",K=637)


I want to creat a "unmarkedFramePCO" with site and obs. covariates. So I first create a matrix with the data (y)

y<-reshape(subset(anapla.dat,select=c("Year","Site","Count")), timevar = "Year",idvar = "Site",direction="wide")

And I do the same for the site covariates

sc1<-reshape(subset(anapla.dat,select=c("Year","Site", "Habitat", "Whole")), timevar = "Year",idvar = "Site",direction="wide")

So far so good.
um.dat.covs<- unmarkedFramePCO(y = y[,2:30], siteCovs = sc1[2:59] , numPrimary=T)

This works.
But when I try to do the same with the obsCovs, it gives me different errors.

According to the help, a data frame with Year, site and Cov1 and another data frame with Year, Site and Cov2 and then do something like:

oc1<- list(Boat.dataframe, Scope.dataframe)
and then use it:

um.dat.covs<- unmarkedFramePCO(y = y[,2:30], siteCovs = sc1[2:59] , obsCovs = oc1, numPrimary=T)

This gives me an error. Am I interpreting wrongly the help file?

Error in unmarkedFramePCO(y = y[, 2:30], siteCovs = sc1[2:59], obsCovs = oc,  : 
  At least one matrix in obsCovs has incorrect number of dimensions.

If I tried the same approach than with the SiteCovs:
oc1<-reshape(subset(anapla.dat,select=c("Year","Site","Boat","Scope")), timevar = "Year",idvar = "Site", direction="wide")

The it gives me another error:
Error in validObject(.Object) : 
  invalid class “unmarkedFrame” object: obsCovData does not have M*obsNum rows.


So, how should I code my obsCovs to be able to create the object unmarkedFramePCO? By the way, the two variables that I want to have as obsCovs are two categorical variables related to the survey approach (by boat (yes/no); spoting scope used (yes/no)

Thank you so much in advance.

Diego

whole <- sc1[,paste("Whole", 1986:2014, sep=".")]
um.dat.covs<- unmarkedFramePCO(y = y[,2:30],

parts:
Hi Diego,

There are 3 processes that you can model with pcountOpen: (1) spatial variation in initial abundance, (2) spatio-temporal variation in abundance after year 1, and (3) detection conditional on abundance. If you want to model the effect of habitat and whole on all years, then you need model both initial abundance using siteCovs and subsequent abundance using yearlySiteCovs. You only need obsCovs if you have robust design data.

Richard

Hi Diego,

There are 3 processes that you can model with pcountOpen: (1) spatial variation in initial abundance, (2) spatio-temporal variation in abundance after year 1, and (3) detection conditional on abundance. Richard

parts: Hi Diego, you didn't specify any covariates in the model formula.  You can create a single unmarked frame with all covariates included and keep that for all analyses.  When you want to fit different model structures, you need to specify which covariates are associated with which parameters, whether no covariates (~1) or some combination (~covariate1 + covariate2) using different calls to the pcountOpen function.  And you need to read the help file to determine the order of parameters, to ensure the covariate specification is correct.
